articles.title: Helicóptero lança 'chuva de sementes' para recuperar palmeira ameaçada | G1
articles.standfirst: Foram dispersadas 2,6 milhões de sementes em 80 hectares em Rio Novo do Sul. Do fruto da juçara é possível extrair a polpa para fazer suco (estilo açaí), bebidas, doces e pratos salgados.
articles.summary: Foram dispersados 2,6 milhões de sementes em 80 hectares em Rio Novo do Sul. Do fruto da juçara é possível extrair a polpa para suco (estilo açaí), bebidas, doces e pratos salgados
articles.body:
Cerca de quatro toneladas de sementes de palmeira-juçara ( Euterpe edulis ) foram lançadas de um helicóptero em uma operação inédita que busca recuperar e reflorestar a Mata Atlântica em uma área de difícil acesso em Rio Novo do Sul , no Sul do Espírito Santo.

Além da preservação ambiental, o objetivo é fortalecer a economia local, já que a espécie é usada para diferentes finalidades. Do fruto da juçara é possível extrair a polpa para fazer um suco 'estilo' açaí, bebidas, doces e pratos salgados.

As sementes usadas na operação nasceram na própria região e foram doadas por proprietários de três agroindústrias locais de polpa de juçara. A aeronave usada na ação foi do Núcleo de Operações e Transporte Aéreo (Notaer).

A escolha por matrizes nativas aumenta as chances de adaptação e germinação das futuras mudas na floresta, um cuidado técnico que promete acelerar a regeneração natural nos próximos anos.

Helicóptero lança 4 toneladas de sementes de juçara para reflorestar área de Mata Atlântica e recuperar espécie de palmeira ameaçada no Espírito Santo — Foto: Reprodução/TV Gazeta

Um dos personagens dessa história é o produtor de mudas Natalino Marquezini, que enxerga na operação o reforço de um trabalho que já realizava de forma artesanal. Ele explicou que a espécie exige atenção constante no manejo:

"Ela é um pouco melindrosa e muito complicada. A juçara depende do tempo: se der muito sol, ela não germina; se tiver muita chuva ou muita água, ela vai apodrecer", comenta o produtor.

Apesar dos desafios, Natalino confia na recuperação do ecossistema local: "Se todo mundo fizer a sua parte semeando, a gente vai conseguir. Eu acredito que vai melhorar 100%".

Ameaça de extinção e o ciclo da 'mãe da floresta'

Por trás do sobrevoo existe também uma corrida contra o tempo. A palmeira-juçara está classificada como vulnerável à extinção na lista oficial do Sistema de Informação sobre a Biodiversidade Brasileira (SiBBr), principalmente devido ao histórico de extração ilegal de palmito.

Diferentemente de espécies como a pupunha, a juçara possui caule único. Quando cortada para a retirada do palmito, a planta morre definitivamente e não volta a brotar, o que enquadra a prática como crime ambiental.

Na natureza, a dispersão da espécie depende da fauna silvestre. Por alimentar dezenas de aves e mamíferos e ser indispensável para o equilíbrio do bioma , a árvore é apelidada por biólogos e ambientalistas de 'mãe da floresta' ou 'arroz e feijão da Mata Atlântica'.

Helicóptero lança 4 toneladas de sementes de juçara para reflorestar área de Mata Atlântica — Foto: Reprodução/TV Gazeta

Com a planta praticamente ausente do trecho sobrevoado devido à degradação e ao desmate predatório do passado, o ciclo natural de regeneração estava interrompido.

De acordo com engenheiros e técnicos do Instituto Capixaba de Pesquisa, Assistência Técnica e Extensão Rural (Incaper), a dispersão aérea com helicóptero vem justamente para acelerar o processo.

A expectativa dos pesquisadores é que, em um período de 5 a 6 anos, a quantidade de árvores adultas tenha crescido consideravelmente na região, permitindo que os próprios animais voltem a espalhar as sementes sozinhos.

No ar, a operação seguiu um rigoroso protocolo técnico. O helicóptero sobrevoou uma área de aproximadamente 80 hectares de mata fechada e de terreno acidentado.

"É uma área densa, de mata virgem, fechada, de aproximadamente 80 hectares. Escolhemos o local devido à inexistência da palmeira-juçara na floresta e pela proximidade", explicou o secretário municipal de Agricultura e Meio Ambiente de Rio Novo do Sul, Gustavo Lourencini.

Um sistema de GPS orientou as faixas de voo para garantir a distribuição uniforme de aproximadamente 2,6 milhões de sementes sobre o terreno. A escolha pela via aérea permitiu cobrir a área sem a necessidade de abrir trilhas ou pisotear a vegetação nativa.

Inspirada no Programa Pró-Juçara, da Fundação Florestal de São Paulo, a ação foi realizada pela prefeitura em parceria com o Incaper e o Notaer.

Fruto movimenta o 'açaí capixaba' e a economia local

Reconhecida por lei estadual como a Capital Estadual da Juçara , Rio Novo do Sul tem transformado a conservação da espécie em oportunidade de negócio. A polpa do fruto, apelidada de 'açaí capixaba', virou a principal fonte de renda para produtores de sorvetes, picolés e doces artesanais na região.

A empresária Drielem Perim Menegardo destacou a relevância social da atividade no meio rural.

"Hoje, a gente trabalha com mais de 60 pessoas no ramo da juçara. Ela não traz renda só para a minha família, mas para toda a comunidade de Rio Novo do Sul", comemora Drielem.

O alcance do ingrediente ultrapassou os limites municipais. A polpa produzida na cidade ganhou espaço em cozinhas autorais e restaurantes dentro e fora do estado, tornando-se o atrativo principal da Rota da Juçara, circuito turístico e gastronômico que conecta Rio Novo do Sul a Vargem Alta.

Conscientização nas escolas e legado para o futuro

O impacto da preservação da juçara também ganhou as salas de aula da rede municipal. Para ensinar aos estudantes que a palmeira representa mais do que uma celebração festiva, a pedagoga Dolores Paixão ajudou a criar um projeto educativo focado no valor ambiental e econômico da espécie.

"Para as crianças deixarem de ver a palmeira apenas como 'a festa da juçara', nós criamos um projeto que leva até elas a importância da geração de renda para o nosso município", explica a professora.

A nova geração de estudantes vai acompanhar de perto os frutos do reflorestamento aéreo. O produtor Natalino Marquezini prevê resultados visíveis em médio prazo: "Daqui a cinco anos, o pessoal já vai ver cachos de juçara espalhados pela região".

Crianças mostram sementes da juçara — Foto: Reprodução/TV Gazeta

Para Drielem, o valor real da ação está na garantia de sustentabilidade para as próximas gerações:

"Eu falava muito sobre isso: quando a gente vier a faltar, quem vai manter essa floresta viva? Hoje estamos vendo essa dispersão aérea, e isso é gigante. Não é só para mim. Daqui a 10 ou 15 anos, os meus filhos e os filhos de todos os produtores vão ter essa renda. A juçara não vai morrer, vai se manter viva", desabafa a empresária.

Segundo a Prefeitura de Rio Novo do Sul, o voo integrou conservação ambiental, inovação tecnológica e agricultura familiar em uma única iniciativa.

A gestão municipal espera que o projeto sirva de modelo para futuras ações de restauração ecológica por dispersão aérea em outros trechos degradados da Mata Atlântica capixaba.

*Texto adaptado por Kamila Rossi, aluna do 29º Curso de Residência em Jornalismo. Este conteúdo teve orientação e edição de Vitor Ferri.

articles.title: Congado em Uberlândia: a hierarquia dos ternos nos 150 anos da festa | G1
articles.standfirst: Entenda como funciona a estrutura por trás da festa do Congado e saiba quantos e quais são os ternos de Uberlândia.
articles.summary: Com 150 anos de história, o Congado em Uberlândia mantém uma hierarquia rigorosa entre os 24 ternos que preservam a cultura afro-brasileira na região.
articles.body:
Quem acompanha os cortejos do Congado pelas ruas de Uberlândia se encanta com as cores, os cantos, os sons e a dança da festa que chega aos 150 anos neste final de semana. Mas, por trás dessa manifestação religiosa e cultural de matriz africana, que em Uberlândia antecede até a história cultural da cidade , existe uma estrutura própria de organização, composta por hierarquias, funções e conhecimentos transmitidos entre gerações.

Essa tradição, que se tornou Patrimônio Cultural Imaterial do Brasil em 2025 , é cheia de curiosidades. Por exemplo, é congado ou congada? O que faz um capitão? O que é um terno?

O g1 entrevistou o historiador e pesquisador das culturas tradicionais afro-brasileiras Jeremias Brasileiro e a relações públicas da Irmandade de Nossa Senhora do Rosário e São Benedito (INSRSB), Tayrine Rodrigues para mostrar mais sobre a preparação para a festa que envolve meses de trabalho.

Cada grupo tem suas tradições. Cargos como capitão, madrinha e general representam reconhecimento dentro da trajetória religiosa e cultural dos congadeiros. Saiba mais sobre a festa e entenda as funções de cada um e quais são as principais características do Congado em Uberlândia.

Os dois termos estão corretos. Congada é usada para se referir aos festejos, enquanto Congado designa o conjunto das expressões religiosas e culturais ligadas a essa tradição de matriz africana.

Segundo a Irmandade, a celebração era realizada originalmente em novembro porque os negros e os grupos de Congado não podiam participar da Festa de Nossa Senhora do Rosário promovida pela antiga irmandade formada por pessoas brancas, realizada em 7 de outubro.

Com o fim da Irmandade de Nossa Senhora do Rosário dos Brancos e, consequentemente, da Festa da padroeira em outubro, o padre Marcelo Augelo, então pároco da Catedral de Santa Teresinha, propôs que a Festa da Congada fosse transferida para outubro. Segundo Jeremias Brasileiro, a mudança foi aprovada pela assembleia da INSRSB em data não informada e, desde então, a celebração ocorre na primeira quinzena do mês.

Terno Sainha é o mais antigo de Uberlândia, foi fundado em 1888 — Foto: Larissa Lali/Divulgação

Os ternos são os grupos que participam da celebração. A origem de cada um está ligada a contextos e necessidades específicas da comunidade congadeira, o que faz com que cada grupo tenha sua própria história. Neste ano, em Uberlândia, participam os 24 ternos da cidade e dois convidados.

Segundo a Irmandade, o terno mais antigo da cidade é o Sainha, formado em 1888, e os mais novo o Moçambique Quilombo dos Palmares, de 2007 sendo incorporado à irmandade em 2017.

Uma pessoa pode fundar um terno desde que tenha reconhecimento por sua trajetória religiosa e cultural no Congado. No caso da filiação à INSRSB, é necessário cumprir exigências previstas no estatuto e no regimento da entidade, além da aprovação da assembleia geral.

Diferentemente das escolas de samba, os ternos não são divididos em alas. A organização segue uma hierarquia militar tradicional formada por bandeireiras, madrinhas, soldados, capitães, generais e guardinhas.

Representam o reinado e ocupam posições de destaque nas celebrações. Participam dos cortejos e de cerimônias religiosas que valorizam a ancestralidade e a tradição afro-brasileira. Em Uberlândia tem-se uma característica fundamental que diferencia o festejo: tanto casal do Reinado Perpétuo, quanto dos Reinados Festeiros escolhidos anualmente, são pertencentes à comunidade do Congado.

Responsáveis por liderar o terno. Orientam os integrantes, conduzem os cantos e coordenam os movimentos e os ritmos durante os cortejos. Também exercem um papel importante na transmissão dos conhecimentos e das tradições do grupo.

3. General ou comandante-geral (leia mais abaixo)

Em algumas festas, é a pessoa responsável por representar e orientar o conjunto dos ternos. Pode atuar na organização dos cortejos, na recepção das guardas e na condução de momentos coletivos da celebração. As atribuições variam conforme a organização de cada festa.

São as pessoas responsáveis pela música que acompanha os cortejos. Tocam instrumentos de percussão como caixas ou harmonia, conforme o estilo do terno. Os ritmos orientam os movimentos e acompanham os cantos.

Formam as fileiras do terno e executam os movimentos coreográficos. Também acompanham os cantos e os ritmos conduzidos pela liderança. Em algumas guardas, as danças incluem movimentos com bastões ou outros elementos característicos daquele estilo.

Em alguns ternos, é uma pessoa experiente que auxilia na condução dos movimentos e dos ritmos. Pode ajudar a orientar os demais integrantes durante as apresentações e os cortejos. A função e o nome variam entre os grupos.

Carregam a bandeira que identifica o terno ou traz a imagem do santo de devoção. O objeto tem importância simbólica e religiosa e participa de momentos específicos do cortejo.

Na festa do Congado em Uberlândia, a guia é a bandeira que vai na frente dos ternos guiando o caminho.

Atualmente, a INSRSB reúne 24 ternos distribuídos entre Congos, Marujos, Marinheiros, Catupés e Moçambiques. O mais antigo é o Terno Sainha. Os mais recentes são o Catupé do Mansour e o Moçambique Quilombo dos Palmares.

Desde 2021, a filiação de novos ternos à irmandade está suspensa e permanecerá assim até 2042, conforme o estatuto da instituição.

Jeremias Brasileiro em 2006, quando chegou assumiu o papel de general na Congada Uberlândia — Foto: Fabíola Benfica/Divulgação

O historiador e pesquisador Jeremias Brasileiro ocupa a função de general da festa da Congada em Uberlândia há duas décadas. Segundo ele, o general atua como comandante-geral e orador da festa, sendo responsável por receber, na Igreja do Rosário, as bandeiras dos diversos grupos participantes, mantendo uma tradição ligada às antigas representações dos reinos do Congo e de Angola.

De acordo com Jeremias, a transmissão do conhecimento ocorre por meio do convívio e dos ensinamentos dos mais velhos. Ele afirma que já pensa na preparação das futuras gerações para garantir a continuidade da tradição e preservar a ancestralidade ligada à festa.

Jeremias conta que chegou em Uberlândia em 1974 e se aproximou da festa em 1985. Nos anos 2000 começou a conversar com o Tio Cândido e o senhor Adenir Nascimento, que lhe passaram conhecimentos valiosos.

"Eu não sabia, mas eles estavam me preparando para essa função. Para a transição, temos o Aliester, tataraneto de Teófilo Nascimento, comandante em 1930. Pode ser que o próximo general venha com essa ancestralidade familiar", disse Jeremias Brasileiro.

A Irmandade de Nossa Senhora do Rosário e São Benedito de Uberlândia é a instituição que reúne e representa os diferentes ternos do Congado na cidade. Ela organiza e apoia as celebrações religiosas em homenagem aos santos, preserva as tradições afro-brasileiras e cuida da Igreja de Nossa Senhora do Rosário e São Benedito. Os ternos mantêm sua própria organização, enquanto a Irmandade atua como representante do conjunto dos grupos.

A história da instituição está ligada à organização de pessoas negras que, ainda no século XIX, promoviam as festas do Congado e a devoção a Nossa Senhora do Rosário. Oficializada em 1916 , a Irmandade também tem um papel importante na preservação da memória e da identidade cultural dessas comunidades. Atualmente, reúne ternos de Congo, Moçambique, Catupé, Marujos e Marinheiros, contribuindo para a continuidade da tradição entre as gerações.

articles.title: O que se sabe sobre ataque a aeroporto na Arábia Saudita que matou 12 e feriu mais de 300 | G1
articles.standfirst: O ataque de sábado foi o mais mortal na Arábia Saudita desde maio de 2015. Autoridades americanas e sauditas culpam os houthis do Iêmen, que ainda não se pronunciaram sobre o ataque.
articles.summary: O ataque de sábado foi o mais mortal na Arábia Saudita desde maio de 2015. Autoridades americanas e sauditas culpam os houthis do Iêmen, que ainda não se pronunciaram sobre o ataque.
articles.body:
Ambulâncias se deslocaram para o aeroporto de Riad para atender os feridos — Foto: REUTERS

Entre as vítimas fatais, estavam quatro sauditas, duas pessoas de Bangladesh e cidadãos de Estados Unidos, Jordânia, Palestina, Síria, Sudão e Egito, confirmou a autoridade de aviação civil saudita.

As operações no Aeroporto Internacional Rei Khalid foram suspensas após o ataque, o mais mortal no reino desde maio de 2015.

Uma coalizão militar liderada pela Arábia Saudita prometeu responder ao ataque, que classificou como um "crime de guerra" e atribuiu aos houthis do Iêmen .

Os houthis não comentaram o ataque de sábado, mas afirmaram ser os responsáveis pelos ataques ao mesmo aeroporto na quinta-feira, que mataram três pessoas e danificaram um avião.

Outras três pessoas foram mortas em ataques dos houthis em dois aeroportos diferentes da Arábia Saudita , nos dias 6 e 7 de outubro.

Os confrontos entre as forças governamentais do Iêmen , apoiadas pela Arábia Saudita , e os houthis, que são apoiados pelo Irã e controlam a maior parte do país, se intensificaram recentemente.

Além dos ataques ao aeroporto de Riad, um projétil também caiu perto do Aeroporto Internacional Rei Fahd, em Dammam, no leste da Arábia Saudita , no sábado, informou a coalizão liderada pelos sauditas.

Em comunicado divulgado no sábado, a autoridade de aviação civil saudita afirmou que alguns dos feridos estavam "em estado crítico" e que os danos ao aeroporto estavam sendo avaliados.

Mais de uma dúzia de ambulâncias foram vistas se deslocando para o aeroporto, disse uma testemunha à agência de notícias Reuters.

O porta-voz da coalizão liderada pela Arábia Saudita , major-general Turki al-Maliki, afirmou que o ataque a um dos terminais de passageiros resultou em mortes e feridos entre passageiros civis e funcionários do aeroporto.

Ele descreveu o ataque como um "crime de guerra em todos os sentidos".

Uma testemunha ocular disse à Reuters que viu "pessoas feridas diante dos meus olhos" fugindo do portão 401 após o ataque.

António Guterres, Secretário-Geral das Nações Unidas, disse estar "profundamente chocado" com os ataques, que classificou como uma "violação do direito internacional" que "deve cessar imediatamente".

Em um comunicado divulgado na página X, o Ministério das Relações Exteriores do Kuwait classificou os ataques como um "ataque hediondo e covarde". Os ataques também foram condenados pelo Egito, Palestina e Catar.

O secretário de Estado dos EUA, Marco Rubio, condenou veementemente os recentes ataques à Arábia Saudita e confirmou a morte de um cidadão americano nos atentados.

Em declarações à imprensa, o presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, indicou que poderá se juntar aos sauditas na realização de ataques contra os houthis, grupo apoiado pelo Irã.

"Acabamos de tomar conhecimento do ataque recente, então tomaremos uma decisão. Agimos com muita rapidez."

Pela segunda vez em menos de um mês, as escolas de Riad passaram a adotar o ensino remoto durante esta semana.

As embaixadas ocidentais na Arábia Saudita alertaram seus cidadãos para que se mantivessem afastados do aeroporto de Riad. O Ministério das Relações Exteriores do Reino Unido orientou os cidadãos britânicos a evitarem a área "até que o aeroporto esteja seguro". A embaixada dos EUA informou aos seus funcionários que eles devem solicitar "autorização especial" para utilizar os aeroportos de Riad, Jidá e Dammam.

Diversas companhias aéreas do Golfo disseram ter cancelado seus voos partindo ou chegando ao aeroporto, com a Kuwait Airways citando a "situação de segurança" no local.

Os houthis afirmam que estão visando a Arábia Saudita devido ao apoio que o país oferece às forças governamentais na guerra civil do Iêmen .

O conflito se agravou depois que os houthis tomaram trechos estrategicamente importantes da costa do Mar Vermelho em uma rápida ofensiva.

Isso incluía o porto de Mokha, no estreito de Bab al-Mandab, o ponto mais estreito do Mar Vermelho e um gargalo para a navegação global. As forças pró-governo iemenitas afirmaram posteriormente ter "garantido" o controle do estreito na extremidade sul do Mar Vermelho.

A coalizão liderada pela Arábia Saudita foi formada em 2015, depois que países árabes uniram forças para impedir que os houthis tomassem o poder no Iêmen , destituindo o governo internacionalmente reconhecido do país.

Um cessar-fogo temporário foi negociado em 2022, após anos de ataques aéreos e combates terrestres que resultaram na morte de centenas de milhares de pessoas, desencadeando uma das piores crises humanitárias do mundo.

Mas a trégua informal começou a ruir em julho.

Os houthis anunciaram um "embargo marítimo" contra a Arábia Saudita e iniciaram ataques com mísseis e drones contra aeroportos, instalações petrolíferas e navios-tanque sauditas no Mar Vermelho.

Eles disseram que estavam retaliando contra o que descreveram como um bloqueio saudita que já durava anos e contra um ataque aéreo ao aeroporto de Sanaa, capital do Iêmen , que é controlada pelos houthis.

Os houthis são um grupo político e religioso armado do norte do Iêmen que defende a minoria muçulmana xiita do país, os zaiditas.

Eles se declaram parte do "eixo da resistência" liderado pelo Irã contra Israel, os EUA e o Ocidente em geral, juntamente com grupos armados como o Hamas e o movimento Hezbollah do Líbano.

As últimas trocas de mensagens ocorrem em meio a temores de que os EUA e Israel possam estar prestes a retomar os ataques contra o Irã. Os esforços para garantir um acordo que ponha fim a esse conflito, que provocou ondas de choque na economia global, até agora não deram resultado.

articles.title: Milionários cubanos em Miami planejam retorno após queda do regime | G1
articles.standfirst: Os exilados cubanos na Flórida vivem expectativa cada vez maior de mudanças no regime de Cuba no futuro próximo.
articles.summary: Exilados cubanos em Miami articulam planos de investimento e infraestrutura para uma possível transição política e econômica na ilha após o fim do regime.
articles.body:
Juan Omar Sixto afirma que ele e seus colegas estão prontos para 'ir fazer negócios em Cuba imediatamente' — Foto: BBC

Na suntuosa mansão com vista para a baía de Biscayne de um dos cirurgiões plásticos de maior prestígio de Miami , nos Estados Unidos , reúnem-se algumas da famílias cubano-americanas mais ricas da Flórida.

Eles estão ali para debater o futuro de Cuba , na quarta reunião da recém-criada Câmara Nacional de Comércio Cubano-Americana (Cancc, na sigla em inglês).

Com um copo de rum na mão e um Rolex no pulso, esta é a velha aristocracia de Miami .

Pessoas com sobrenomes cubano-americanos muito conhecidos, como Bacardí e Babún, conversam em torno da piscina sobre o lamentável estado da economia da ilha e compartilham fofocas sobre os últimos acontecimentos políticos.

"A intenção desta noite é reunir sob o mesmo teto os empresários cubano-americanos mais destacados do condado de Miami -Dade", explica Juan Omar Sixto, presidente da Cancc.

"O objetivo é estar em Cuba assim que cair o regime", segundo ele. E seus convidados estão convencidos de que este momento está chegando.

Esta influente comunidade de exilados cubanos odeia o governo comunista da ilha, desde que o líder revolucionário Fidel Castro (1926-2016) expropriou suas terras e nacionalizou as empresas das suas famílias, ao tomar o poder em Cuba em 1959.

Ao longo dos anos, eles usaram sua influência política e econômica na Flórida para moldar as políticas de Washington em relação ao seu país de origem.

Sixto fugiu da ilha quando era adolescente. Agora, com pouco mais de 80 anos e dedicado à construção civil, sua organização está elaborando planos para o que ele chama de "dia seguinte" em Cuba .

A Cancc elaborou uma proposta para uma Bolsa de Valores cubana. Ele já formou comitês sobre diversos temas, desde infraestrutura energética até segurança alimentar.

O planejamento para a esperada era pós-comunista não é nada de novo em Miami . Ao longo das décadas, diversos grupos de interesse elaboraram inúmeros documentos e planos logísticos, alguns mais sóbrios e comedidos que outros.

Agora, segundo Sixto, a diferença está no empenho do governo do presidente dos Estados Unidos , Donald Trump , de forçar uma mudança radical na ilha. E ele afirma que os empresários contam com o apoio de contatos influentes, incluindo pessoas próximas ao secretário de Estado americano, Marco Rubio .

"Além de fornecer ajuda humanitária e insumos médicos, iríamos fazer negócios em Cuba imediatamente", garante Sixto.

Em Cuba , este tipo de afirmação costuma ser recebida com ceticismo.

Frente à campanha de "pressão máxima" de Washington sobre Cuba , o governo da ilha anunciou recentemente 176 medidas de liberalização econômica.

O presidente cubano, Miguel Díaz-Canel , declarou que as medidas buscam "promover a defesa do socialismo, apoiar e ampliar a justiça social".

Para seus críticos, estas medidas se assemelham claramente ao capitalismo, na sua expressão máxima. Elas eliminam o limite do número de trabalhadores nas empresas privadas, permitem a contratação e demissão direta de funcionários cubanos e autorizam a propriedade de diversas empresas ao mesmo tempo, incluindo por cidadãos cubano-americanos.

Mas as pessoas que compareceram à reunião da Cancc minimizam as reformas econômicas de Havana. Eles as qualificam de superficiais e consideram que elas não oferecem garantias significativas para os investidores.

Sixto destaca que não colocará um pé em Cuba , enquanto o regime atual permanecer no poder.

Analistas consideram que estas reuniões de planejamento são prematuras. Os cubano-americanos estão convencidos de que a mudança em Cuba é iminente, mas ninguém pode afirmar com certeza no que ela irá consistir.

Será uma operação militar americana, como a que ocorreu na Venezuela, em janeiro? Ou um novo pacto econômico com o governo da ilha?

"Neste momento, as altíssimas expectativas criadas pelo governo americano de que viria em breve uma espécie de 'dia seguinte', ou de que Cuba 'seria a próxima', foram postergadas", destaca o professor de história Mike Bustamante, da Universidade de Miami .

Frente à proximidade das eleições de meio de mandato nos Estados Unidos , em novembro, e com o governo Trump imerso no "atoleiro" da guerra contra o Irã, Bustamante afirma que existe pouco interesse por novas aventuras no exterior.

"Realmente, é difícil pensar que eles irão intensificar a situação além do que já estão fazendo, que é este gotejamento constante de sanções", segundo ele.

O abastecimento de petróleo da ilha, praticamente interrompido desde janeiro , já representa uma escalada significativa, afirma Bustamante.

Para ele, esta situação tornou a vida insuportável para a maior parte das pessoas comuns, mas ainda não criou as condições para uma reviravolta política em Cuba .

O governo cubano não se pronunciou sobre a Cancc propriamente dita. Mas, tradicionalmente, este tipo de grupo provoca indignação entre os revolucionários, que insistem que não serão expulsos pelos seus críticos em Miami .

Pergunto a alguns convidados se eles percebem a ironia de que as mesmas pessoas que apoiam uma das principais causas de angústia na ilha (o embargo econômico americano de décadas e o atual bloqueio do combustível) idealizem planos para sua reconstrução, sem a participação da maioria dos cubanos.

Hugo Orizondo reconhece que é difícil conhecer a situação atual em Cuba — Foto: BBC

Para o especialista agrícola cubano-americano Hugo Orizondo, o mais prático é traçar um caminho para o desenvolvimento de Cuba .

"No momento, Cuba é como um buraco negro", reconhece ele. "Não sabemos o que acontece ali. Mas conhecemos seu potencial" de investimento.

Orizondo afirma que compreende que os cubanos fiquem reticentes ao ver investidores estrangeiros adquirindo algo delicado como os direitos sobre terras agrícolas.

"Mas o que eles vão fazer com elas?", questiona ele. "Quando os investidores chegam, eles trazem dinheiro e tecnologia."

Para Orizondo, ambos são urgentemente necessários para que a produção da ilha atinja níveis suficientes para alimentar sua própria população, eliminando a dependência cubana da importação de alimentos.

Os títulos de propriedade são fundamentais para qualquer projeto de reconstrução proposto pela atual geração de cubano-americanos abastados.

Juan Omar Sixto conta que seu pai perdeu cinco propriedades e uma fazenda na província de Pinar del Río, no oeste de Cuba , devido à revolução.

Ele defende que não tem intenção de desalojar nenhuma família que mora ali, mas exige uma compensação pelas terras nacionalizadas.

"Trabalhei naquela fazenda por cinco anos da minha vida com meu pai e eles a tiraram", prossegue ele. "Quero a restituição ou uma indenização. Mesmo se me derem apenas uma pequena parte, eu a aceitarei. É justiça moral".

O governo cubano qualifica estas reivindicações históricas de títulos de propriedade como atos de ressentimento por parte de uma aristocracia latifundiária corrupta , que acumulou fortunas às custas de servos contratados e pessoas escravizadas.

A servidão por contrato e a escravidão só desapareceram em Cuba no final do século 19.

O governo também defende que os exilados nunca teriam aceitado que Castro aprovasse reformas agrárias que entregassem suas terras aos trabalhadores ou ao Estado.

"A maioria dos nossos engenhos de açúcar foi destruída, mas recuperaremos aquelas terras e as colocaremos em produção", afirma Nicolás Gutiérrez, presidente da Associação Nacional de Proprietários de Engenhos Açucareiros de Cuba , uma organização no exílio que defende as reivindicações dos antigos proprietários.

"Não prometo que seja em açúcar", reconhece ele. "Poderia ser etanol, cogeração, painéis solares ou células de purificação de água."

"Quem sabe? Existem muitas opções", afirma Gutiérrez.

"Precisamos que elas comecem a produzir, precisamos que seja pago um salário justo aos trabalhadores cubanos, criando um efeito multiplicador na economia de toda a ilha."

Com gelo tilintando nas bebidas e uma brisa fresca balançando as palmeiras no gramado impecavelmente cuidado, os membros da Cancc fazem tudo parecer fácil.

Mas, a poucas horas da sua reunião, Cuba mergulhou no seu sexto apagão nacional do ano.

A desconexão entre as esperanças de mudança em Miami e a realidade em Cuba é evidente. Muitos cubanos residentes na Flórida acreditam que a mudança transcendental que eles rezam para ocorrer está a ponto de chegar.

Se isso acontecer, inevitavelmente, haverá enormes transtornos sociais e humanitários que a ilha, já em dificuldades, não está preparada para enfrentar.

Supondo que o apoio da diáspora seja bem intencionado e não puramente egoísta, estima-se que reparar a deficiente rede elétrica da ilha custará entre US$ 8 bilhões e US$ 10 bilhões (cerca de R$ 40 bilhões a 50 bilhões).

Antes que qualquer indústria em Cuba , da agricultura ao turismo, possa ser revitalizada graças à riqueza e às conexões políticas dos exilados, os cubanos continuam enfrentando uma grave escassez de alimentos, água, combustível e medicamentos.

E, deixando de lado os ambiciosos planos de Miami , a maioria dos cubanos simplesmente espera que seu dia a dia possa ter alguma melhoria em breve.

articles.title: 'Britain's loneliest dog' finds home after three years in kennels
articles.summary: Sadie is enjoying life with a new family after becoming a social media star.
articles.body:
A dog rescued from a property where she was being kept with 200 others has found a new home after nearly three years in kennels.

Collie cross Sadie was rescued by the RSPCA after being found living in unsuitable conditions in outdoor compounds in Cornwall, the charity said.

The five-year-old dog could not be rehomed immediately due to legal processes. But once cleared for adoption she was still in RSPCA kennels after 1,000 days with staff describing her as "Britain's loneliest dog".

In a bid to find her forever home, they posted a video a day of Sadie on social media. On day 83, Mabel Edge from Westward Ho! in Devon stumbled across one of the clips before decided she would adopt her.

Edge said: "When I first saw the clips of her, I was taken by how sweet she seemed and couldn't believe she'd been waiting for a home for so long.

"I found myself checking back in every day to see what she'd been up to, and said to my partner Al how sad it was that nobody wanted her.

"And then he said, 'well why don't we go and look at her?'"

The couple visited Sadie four times at the RSCPA centre before taking her home.

Edge said: "We knew from speaking to the staff at the branch that Sadie would need patience and understanding, because of her difficult past, but we thought she'd be a lot worse.

"After a couple of visits with us, we could see her slowly letting her guard down and she was just so sweet."

She added: "We knew it wouldn't be easy and we would need to work with Sadie, but we knew we could give her something better than she had in kennels."

Edge said on the long journey home Sadie decided to sit in the footwell of their campervan, rather than in a bed they made for her, "and from that moment it was like she'd been in our lives forever".

The dog's previous owner received a jail sentence and has been banned from owning dogs for life, the RSPCA said.

Sadie's happy ending comes as the RSPCA warned rising levels of multi-animal cases were putting "unprecedented pressure" on its teams with 3,280 cases reported across England and Wales already this year.

The RSPCA said that in 2025 it responded to more than 4,200 incidents involving 10 or more animals at a single address, involving 88,000 animals, with 75 cases of more than 100 animals.

articles.title: History of heartbreak exhibition opens in Oxford
articles.summary: A new exhibition in Oxford attempts to chart the history of loves lost through various art mediums.
articles.body:
From Rick and Ilsa's final farewell in Casablanca to Adele singing Someone Like You - heartbreak has been at the heart of popular culture for much of the last century.

But the pain is just about as old as human's themselves. For thousands of years it has provided inspiration for tales of woe and even cause for medical enquiries.

A new exhibition in Oxford is attempting to chart some of that history - tracing back to uncover how people in the past valued, expressed, and tried to recover from the anguish of heartbreak.

After Love, at the OVADA Gallery in the city centre, has been compiled and organised by Sally Holloway, who is a a historian of emotions at the University of Warwick.

"It's something that as a society, we need to be talking about more and we need to be taking it much more seriously," Holloway said of the exhibition's subject matter.

"What I really want to convey with this project is that heartbreak wasn't just a sort of serious physical threat for people in the past, but it can be today too."

The exhibition in Oxford charts the evolution of lost love over the past 400 years, and what that now looks like in 2026.

"I started planning out my next book project and thinking about perhaps I could do something on heartbreak," Holloway said of her latest work.

"As soon as I decided this, I felt like I became the repository for other people's stories of heartbreak - suddenly everybody was coming to me with their own individual story of a breakup, a romantic loss."

"I realised then that I was onto something that happened in the past which had real resonance for people in the present."

The gallery features more than a hundred different works in a various mediums, including film, sculpture and collage.

"I'm starting in early modern England and tracing the changing ways that heartbreak was experienced and understood and valued right through to the present day," Holloway explained.

She said the project was "thinking about all the different feelings involved to show really that heartbreak was more than grief".

"For early modern people, the healthy body was a body that was was balanced - so if you were heartbroken you might be experiencing an excess of sadness."

"[It was thought] that sort of degree of emotional strain could cause your heartstrings to literally snap."

"Whereas, by the 18th century heartbroken people spoke of heartbreak more in terms of it was sort of the loss of the meaning of their life."

"Then in the 19th century, people increasingly figured their heartbreak in terms of things like misery and trouble and feelings of shame."

The After Love exhibition at Oxford's OVADA Gallery opened this week, and runs every Thursday to Sunday until 18 October.

Holloway said she had "learned a lot" from working with the more than 50 artists artists involved in the presentation.

"In some ways, heartbreak is an opportunity because it's such a great rupture with the past that it provides that opportunity to look ahead at your own future and ask 'who am I now and what should I do next?'," she added.

articles.title: North East charities and businesses wrestle with diesel cost
articles.summary: Cancer charity Daft as a Brush and Teesside Minibus Hire say they are struggling with pump prices.
articles.body:
Charities and businesses across the North East have said they are struggling with the rising cost of diesel.

The average price of diesel has risen above £2 a litre in the UK for the first time, according to the RAC motoring group .

Over the past seven months, the Iran war has severely disrupted the production and transportation of wholesale oil and refined products from the region, causing prices to surge worldwide.

The North East cancer charity Daft as a Brush said it could no longer afford to upgrade its diesel vehicles to electric as they grappled with filling them up, whilst Teesside Minibus Hire said soaring prices were "not sustainable".

Daft as a Brush, which provides cancer patients with transport to their hospital appointments, said it was shelling out £15,000 a month on diesel - £5,000 more than last year.

The Newcastle-based charity - which drives 600,000 miles every year in its 30 vans - said it had planned on replacing them with electric vehicles, but now could not afford to because the money was being swallowed up at the pump.

Volunteer driver Davey Hall said: "Before the big hikes, we used to maybe fill up and it would take £40-45.

"Last week, it was £94 to fill the tank from half full."

Head of income generation Scott Jobson said the money was being taken from funds raised by donations, and they were not eligible for any kind of discount.

"At the pump, what you see is what we pay," he said.

In Middlesbrough, Teesside Minibus Hire director Billy Johnson said they often signed contracts with schools and businesses which could span multiple years - and were based on the cost of fuel when they were written.

"We're not running at a loss yet, but we're running close it to it not being worthwhile or sustainable," he said.

Johnson said they were having to pass the cost on to customers using services such as day hires, but because those customers were struggling with inflation themselves, they were not always prepared to pay the increased price.

Instead, people were turning towards cheaper, unlicensed hire services which did not pay the same overheads, he said.

Asked whether the business could survive if fuel prices did not drop, he said: "Long term, probably not."

In May , the government announced it would extend a fuel duty (tax) freeze until the end of the year.

It caps the tax at 5p per litre for petrol and diesel, and was introduced by the previous Conservative government after Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine pushed prices up in 2022.

The government has stressed that there is no cause for concern about potential diesel shortages over the Iran War and has said the country has a "diverse and resilient supply".

articles.title: Surrey County Council exceeds its tree planting target
articles.summary: A report finds some 885,000 trees have been planted, but there are concerns over survival rates.
articles.body:
More than 800,000 new trees have been planted across Surrey over the past five years, exceeding the council's own target, according to a report.

Surrey County Council's report found 116,359 trees had been planted in the 2025/26 financial year alone.

It said the total planted between 2021 and 2026 was around 885,000, surpassing its initial target of 600,000.

However, Elmbridge Borough Council recently passed a motion calling for the future East Surrey council to update its tree strategy to consider survival rates.

It said many trees planted in the borough were dying within a year as a result of not receiving the right aftercare.

"There is little point celebrating the number of trees we plant if a significant number of them are dead a year later," said councillor Katerina Lusk.

Surrey County Council has committed to 1.2 million trees being planted by 2030, representing one for every resident.

The authority's report looked at the progress of its climate change delivery programme over the past five years.

It said the council was "broadly on track" to meet its 2030 net zero targets, stating that its carbon emissions have been reduced by around 60%.

The report said: "A major success of the programme has been supporting residents to reduce energy bills and improve their homes.

"More than 1,438 low-income households received energy efficiency improvements, including insulation, solar and low-carbon heating measures."

It also acknowledged challenges ahead in continuing to pursue decarbonisation policies.

The programme was "significantly affected by external market conditions, supply chain constraints and wider economic pressures", it added.

articles.title: Shraddha Walkar murder case: Delhi court allows online testimony of WhatsApp, Google, Bumble officials
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: A Delhi court has allowed Delhi Police to record the testimony of nodal officers of WhatsApp, Google, Gmail and Bumble through video
articles.body: NEW DELHI: A Delhi court has allowed Delhi Police to record the testimony of nodal officers of WhatsApp, Google, Gmail and Bumble through video conferencing from abroad in the Shraddha Walkar murder case, in which Aaftab Amin Poonawala is facing trial.The court said securing the physical presence of the witnesses would involve considerable expense and delay, and directed that their depositions be recorded from December 1, 2026, with one witness examined each day.Additional Sessions Judge (ASJ) Hargurvarinder Singh Jaggi allowed the prosecution's application on Saturday, noting that the witnesses are based in the United States and the United Kingdom. The trial is nearing its conclusion. Court allows online testimony of foreign tech officials"Having considered the application and given that these witnesses reside abroad, securing their physical attendance before this Court would entail undue delay and exorbitant expense. In the interest of an expeditious trial and justice, the application moved by the prosecution is allowed," ASJ Jaggi ordered on Saturday.The court directed that a copy of the order be forwarded to the Consulate General of India, the High Commission of India, the Joint Secretary, CPV (Consular, Passport and Visa) Division of the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA), and the nodal authority of the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) for information and necessary compliance.WhatsApp, Google, Gmail and Bumble officials named as witnessesThe prosecution sought to examine foreign nodal officers who are required to tender evidence through affidavits under Section 296 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (CrPC), and the corresponding provisions of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.The witnesses identified by Delhi Police are:- Adrian Silvera, nodal officer for WhatsApp LLC and Meta Platforms Inc., residing at 1 Hacker Way, Menlo Park, California, USA.- Shelby Smith, nodal officer for Google LLC, based in Austin, Texas, USA.- Arti Sheth, nodal officer for Google (Gmail), whose office is at 1600 Amphitheatre Parkway, Mountain View, California 94043, USA.- Luke Mitsi, nodal officer and law enforcement operations manager for Bumble Group, whose office is at 2 Sheraton Street, London, United Kingdom.Delhi court sets up video-conferencing arrangements for foreign witnessesThe court directed that the Court Point for recording the depositions would be the video-conferencing courtroom of the South District at Saket Courts Complex in Delhi.The Remote Point for each summoned witness will be the nearest Indian embassy or high commission corresponding to the witness's residential or official address.An official designated by the respective Indian embassy, high commission or consulate general will act as the Remote Point Coordinator.Inspector Ram Singh, the investigating officer in the case, has been authorised to act as a liaison officer to ensure that all necessary permissions and authorisations are processed through the appropriate channels in a time-bound manner.Witness examination to begin on December 1The court specified that the witnesses' testimony would be recorded at the rate of one witness per day, beginning December 1, 2026.The Court Point Coordinator has been directed to prepare a detailed date sheet in coordination with the Remote Point Coordinators, Special Public Prosecutor (SPP) and defence counsel.SPP Madhukar Pandey is appearing for Delhi Police.Court lays down rules for serving summons to foreign witnessesThe court directed that all processes and summons be served on the witnesses through the MHA and MEA in accordance with the law and the prevailing Comprehensive Guidelines for Investigation Abroad and issuance of Letters Rogatory (LRs) or Mutual Legal Assistance (MLA) Requests and Service of Summons, as mandated under Rule 9(5) and Rule 12.It also clarified that the summons must explicitly specify the venue of the Remote Point, the date and time of the deposition, and the requirement for identity proof. articles.title: Colorado veteran Cano Espinoza began covering his home with discarded hubcaps, cans, screen doors and scrap metal in 1980; more than four decades later, Cano's Castle remains a well-known roadside attraction in Antonito
articles.summary: In the small town of Antonito in southern Colorado, United States, a house made from discarded beer cans, hubcaps, screen doors and scrap metal became a
articles.body: In the small town of Antonito in southern Colorado, United States, a house made from discarded beer cans, hubcaps, screen doors and scrap metal became a well-known roadside attraction. According to The Denver Gazette, called Cano's Castle, the structure was built by Dominic “Cano” Espinoza, a Native American Vietnam War veteran who reportedly began working on it in 1980.The personal construction project eventually became a local landmark. Espinoza used materials that others had thrown away, combining them with native volcanic stone to build a complex that stood out from the surrounding homes. Over the years, the unusual structure attracted visitors and became familiar to people living in Antonito, a small town near the New Mexico border.The castle was also Espinoza's home. Known locally as a private man who often travelled around town on his bicycle, he continued to be closely associated with the property. His religious faith was another part of his identity, according to reports about the castle and its builder.However, on January 13, 2022, a major fire damaged the property. The blaze destroyed the residential section of the complex, although Espinoza escaped without injuries. The incident raised concerns about a structure that had been part of the town for more than four decades.A castle of discarded materialsEspinoza reportedly began building Cano's Castle in 1980, using a combination of volcanic stone and materials collected from discarded items. Not relying entirely on conventional building materials, he incorporated objects such as old hubcaps, metal scraps, screen doors and beer cans into the structure.The beer cans were carefully cut and used as part of the castle's exterior. Along with the other metal objects, they gave the building its distinctive appearance. The complex also featured two tall towers known as the King and the Queen.Located on a residential street, the property was not a conventional castle. It was a collection of structures created from salvaged materials, reflecting the work Espinoza had carried out over several decades.His project became known as a form of folk art, a term used for creative work often made outside formal artistic institutions. Cano's Castle attracted attention because of the materials used in its construction and the amount of work involved in creating it.For residents of Antonito, the building was more than an unusual roadside sight. It had stood in their neighbourhood for years, becoming part of the town's identity.When fire destroys Cano's CastleThe castle suffered serious damage when a fire broke out in January 2022. The fire was reported shortly after midnight, and firefighters from Antonito, Romeo, Manassa and La Jara responded to the incident.Emergency crews continued fighting the flames until around 5 am. The main fire was extinguished by late morning, although smaller flare-ups were reported afterwards.Antonito police officer Olga Cortez confirmed that the fire had destroyed the residence within the complex. However, the castle's two prominent towers, the King and the Queen, were not damaged. Espinoza was the only occupant of the property at the time and was not injured.The cause of the fire was under investigation when the incident was reported. Cortez said it might have started in the chimney, although this had not been confirmed.She also said Espinoza had not been fully cooperative with authorities following the incident. Describing his reaction to the damage, Cortez said, “He’s more upset.”Residents recall growing up around the castleThe fire affected people who had known the castle since childhood. Among them was Alex Ponce, who lived in an apartment across the street with his girlfriend and son.Ponce told The Denver Gazette that he woke up to see large flames coming from the property. At first, he believed strong winds were causing the beer cans attached to the structure to make noise. He soon realised that the sound was connected to something far more serious.Having been born in Antonito, Ponce had grown up seeing the castle and had even toured it as a child. Watching the property burn was particularly difficult because it had been a familiar part of his surroundings for so many years.“It’s heartbreaking,” Ponce said by phone, “to see something you’ve known all your life go up in flames.”He also expressed confidence that the local community would come together to help Espinoza rebuild his home and the work he had spent decades creating.Although the January 2022 fire destroyed Espinoza's residence, the castle's two main towers survived. According to a report published by OnlyInYourState in 2023, Espinoza continued living on the property in an off-grid trailer. A later report by The Denver Gazette, in July 2025, continued to describe Cano's Castle as a roadside attraction. It is not confirmed whether fire-damaged residence had been rebuilt.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Inside Israel's plot to kill Hezbollah chief as Netanyahu warned Biden aide would 'jump out of his skin'
articles.summary: Benjamin Netanyahu warned that Jake Sullivan would "jump out of his skin" over Israel's secret plan to assassinate Hassan Nasrallah in Beirut.
articles.body: As Israel prepared to assassinate Hezbollah leader Hassan Nasrallah in September 2024, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his senior defense officials disagreed over whether to notify the Biden administration ahead of the operation, fearing Washington could try to stop the mission, according to Wall Street Journal editorial writer Elliot Kaufman and a second source familiar with the deliberations. "140%, they won't approve of the mission," Netanyahu told senior Israeli defense officials, according to Kaufman, co-author of "In the War Room: The Inside Story of Israel's Fight Against Hamas and the Iranian Axis," who recounted the exchange in an interview with Fox News Digital. Then-Defense Minister Yoav Gallant and IDF Chief of Staff Herzi Halevi favored informing Washington, believing the Americans might support a strike against a Hezbollah leader linked to the deaths of U.S. service members, according to Kaufman. Netanyahu, however, warned that then-U.S. National Security Adviser Jake Sullivan would "jump out of his skin" if he learned of the plans. The disagreement reflected a widening divide between Jerusalem and Washington over Israel's military campaign against Iran's regional proxies, as the Biden administration sought to prevent the fighting from escalating into a broader regional war. 'BIBI'S HAIR ON FIRE': TRUMP-NETANYAHU PUBLIC 'RIFT' MASKED UNIFIED FRONT AGAINST IRAN, ANALYST SAYS Hezbollah: Netanyahu's warning about Washington When Israeli jets struck Hezbollah's headquarters in Beirut on September 27, 2024, the Pentagon said it had received no advance warning. Gallant spoke with then-Defense Secretary Lloyd Austin while the operation was already underway. The strike killed Nasrallah, who had led the Iranian-backed terrorist organization for more than three decades, marking a major turning point in Israel's campaign against Hezbollah, which opened a second front against Israel on October 8, 2023, a day after Hamas' deadly attack in southern Israel, and had since launched repeated rocket and missile attacks on northern Israeli communities. Kaufman argued that Israel had spent nearly a year waiting for American diplomacy to end Hezbollah's attacks on its northern communities, without success. "From Israel's point of view, it had been sitting and waiting for 10, 11 months while Hezbollah had been pounding the north of Israel with rockets and with anti-tank missiles, waiting for American diplomacy to succeed," he said. "It didn't work. Something had to change on the northern front." Kaufman said the confrontation exposed a fundamental difference in how the two governments approached the war. "The United States may not have been in Israel's war room, but it could never be denied a seat at the table when it asked," he said. "What I was told from the Israeli prime minister's office is ‘America's goal is to de-escalate the war. Our goal is to win the war,' and we saw that clash at every point, especially during the Biden administration." VP JD VANCE ADDRESSES US-ISRAEL RELATIONSHIP, WHETHER IRAN IS TRYING TO 'PLAY' THE UNITED STATES October 7: Netanyahu's reluctance and the question of accountability The book, written by Kaufman and Jerusalem Post senior military analyst Yonah Jeremy Bob, also describes how Netanyahu initially resisted launching a full-scale ground invasion of Gaza following the Oct. 7, 2023, Hamas massacre, only to emerge later as one of the strongest advocates for continuing the war. "Prime Minister Netanyahu had just seen the IDF, Israel's military, fail miserably on Oct. 7, and Israel's intelligence services fail miserably on October 7," Kaufman told Fox News Digital. Senior American generals dispatched by President Biden also warned Israeli leaders that a ground invasion could end in military defeat, even in Gaza City, according to Kaufman. Netanyahu eventually approved the ground operation on Oct. 27, 2023, after weeks of internal debate. "Over time, he would gain confidence in the IDF, regain confidence in the military, in Israel's intelligence services, and end up outlasting, exhausting, or simply firing all of his war room rivals," Kaufman said. Kaufman was more critical when asked about Netanyahu's accountability for Oct. 7. "I have spoken to Prime Minister Netanyahu several times in person, even more on the phone. I had a three hour conversation with him extending well past midnight in Israel," Kaufman said. "I have not heard him take responsibility for what happened on October 7th." Instead, Kaufman said, Netanyahu consistently points to the failure of senior military officials to alert him before the Hamas assault began. "What he says is, 6:29. They didn't wake me up until 6:29 in the morning on the day of October 7th," Kaufman recounted. Those remarks came as a new controversy erupted in Israel over the official record of Netanyahu's actions on the morning of the attack. In a lengthy interview broadcast Thursday by Israel's Channel 12, retired Maj. Gen. Avi Gil, who served as Netanyahu's military secretary at the time, said that the prime minister's chief of staff, Tzachi Braverman, attempted to alter the official record of a telephone call between Gil and Netanyahu. EXPERTS URGE EXTREME CAUTION ON IRAN'S 'CROWN JEWEL' HEZBOLLAH — TERROR GROUP WITH US BLOOD ON ITS HANDS Gil said a stenographer told him she had been instructed to change the recorded time of their first secure telephone conversation from 6:40 a.m. to 6:29 a.m. Gil said he had raised concerns about irregular recordkeeping with the attorney general's office in real time. Braverman has acknowledged seeking to change the recorded time but denied wrongdoing. Gil also challenged the completeness of Netanyahu's public account of the events preceding the massacre, saying there were significant gaps between what occurred and what had been presented to the Israeli public and in his written statements. The Likud party dismissed the alleged attempt to falsify the record, saying "the matter had been investigated by police two years earlier and that police had recommended closing the case because it lacked substance." However, prosecutors have not announced a decision to close the case. Gil also said that opportunities to secure hostage agreements earlier in the war had been lost because of political considerations. Asked by Channel 12 whether some hostages who died in captivity could have been brought home alive, Gil replied, "We could have." He indicated that opposition to ceasefires and hostage deals from far-right ministers in Netanyahu's coalition influenced the prime minister's decisions. While acknowledging that senior Israeli military officials believed Netanyahu was prolonging the war for political reasons, Kaufman challenged the argument that political survival was his sole motivation, pointing to Israel's subsequent campaigns against Hezbollah and Iran. "There were real strategic interests to be pursued," he said. "Almost all of the real achievements of this war came later in the war," he said, arguing that the subsequent weakening of Hezbollah, the collapse of the Assad regime in Syria and the attacks on Iran's nuclear facilities complicated claims that continued fighting served only Netanyahu's political interests. IDF ANNOUNCES ELIMINATION OF HEZBOLLAH COMMANDER BEHIND MURDER OF 5 AMERICAN SOLDIERS Iran: How Israel helped convince Trump to strike The book also examines how Israel's early military successes against Iran helped persuade President Donald Trump to authorize U.S. strikes on Iranian nuclear facilities during the 12-day war in June 2025. Kaufman described how a Trump administration official showed him a map of Israeli airstrikes that had opened a route toward Fordow, Iran's heavily fortified underground nuclear facility. According to Kaufman, Israeli military chief Eyal Zamir subsequently made the case directly to Vice President JD Vance that American forces had an extraordinary opportunity to strike. "You have a straight shot to Iran's nuclear sites. You will never have a better opportunity than this," Kaufman said, recounting Zamir's message to Vance. Kaufman said the Israeli military chief told Vance that Israeli aircraft were already operating over the area, but that the U.S. possessed the heavy bunker-busting bombs necessary for the Fordow mission. He credited the vice president with helping secure Trump's final authorization for Operation Midnight Hammer. "Vice President Vance played a critical role in ultimately securing American participation in the highly successful 12-day war," Kaufman said. The account challenges the notion that Trump was reluctantly drawn into the conflict by Netanyahu, Kaufman argued, portraying the president instead as responding to an opportunity created by Israel's demonstrated military capabilities. articles.summary: LUCKNOW: Chaotic scenes unfolded at the Uttar Pradesh Congress Committee (UPCC) headquarters on Sunday as supporters of outgoing state president Ajay Rai
articles.body: LUCKNOW: Chaotic scenes unfolded at the Uttar Pradesh Congress Committee (UPCC) headquarters on Sunday as supporters of outgoing state president Ajay Rai clashed with a group associated with Congress councillor Mamta Chaudhary over clearing a passage for him. The confrontation triggered a heated exchange and a scuffle in which shoes were allegedly used.The confrontation occurred shortly before newly appointed UP Congress president Aradhana Mishra ‘Mona’ arrived to formally assume charge.According to party workers present at the venue, the dispute began when Rai's supporters asked people standing near the entrance to make way, saying the state president was arriving. Chaudhary allegedly responded by asking, "Which president?", provoking an argument between the two groups.The verbal confrontation soon escalated, with supporters from both sides allegedly attacking each other with shoes. Rai's supporters accused Chaudhary of insulting the outgoing president and demanded her expulsion from the party.Sources among party workers claimed Rai was visibly upset by the incident and initially decided to leave the headquarters without participating in the formal handover ceremony.However, following the intervention of Congress MP Imran Masood and incoming president Mona, Rai returned to the premises and formally handed over charge to his successor.Significantly, although Rai participated in the handover, he was conspicuously absent when Mona subsequently addressed her first press conference as UP Congress president.Asked about Rai's departure, Masood maintained that the outgoing president had completed the formalities. "He left only after handing over charge," Masood said.Meanwhile, Uttar Pradesh Mahila Congress vice-president Sheela Mishra offered a different account of the confrontation, claiming that women workers had gathered to welcome both the outgoing and incoming presidents."We were standing there to welcome both leaders. Some young men started asking us to move aside. Mamta merely told them that we were also there to welcome the new president," she said.Sheela alleged that some men then asked the women to "stay within their limits", escalating tensions. She also claimed that banners put up by women workers had been damaged earlier.Describing Rai as a respected leader, she said women Congress workers wanted him to receive a bigger responsibility within the party.Despite the disruption, Mona formally assumed charge and addressed the media, outlining her priorities for strengthening the organisation ahead of the 2027 assembly elections.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Lucknow | Silver Rate in Lucknow | Bank Holidays in Lucknow | Public Holidays in Lucknow | Lucknow AQI | Weather in Lucknow | Petrol Price in Lucknow | Diesel Price in Lucknow | CNG Price in Lucknow | LPG Price in LucknowStay updated with the latest Lucknow news. articles.summary: Polish security services were due to hold an emergency meeting on Sunday after police received information about a possible attack on Prime Minister
articles.body: Polish security services were due to hold an emergency meeting on Sunday after police received information about a possible attack on Prime Minister Donald Tusk and defence minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz, authorities said.The exact nature and origin of the reported threat were not immediately clear. The meeting was ordered by interior minister Marcin Kierwiński and Tomasz Siemoniak, the minister-coordinator of special services, according to a statement posted on X by Interior Ministry spokesperson Karolina Galecka.“Following information received by the Polish Police regarding a possible attack ...interior minister, Marcin Kierwiński, and the minister-coordinator of Special Services, Tomasz Siemoniak, have ordered action to be taken in this matter,” Galecka wrote.She said a meeting would take place at 11 am local time at the Internal Security Agency’s Counter-Terrorism Centre.Private broadcaster Radio Zet reported that police had received an email containing information about the threat.As per news agency AP, police had received information about a possible attack, but authorities had not released further details.Poland on alert after attacks at schoolsThe security alert comes as Polish authorities remain on high alert following a series of violent incidents at schools in the central Mazovian province over four days last week.Three attacks left one person dead and several others injured, including children. On Wednesday, a 19-year-old student at a vocational school wounded nine people, including fellow students, teachers and passersby, with a sharp object. He was arrested nearby.The following day, a 15-year-old killed a school caretaker and wounded two other people in a knife attack at his former school. On Saturday, a 21-year-old woman wounded three people at a post-secondary school in Warsaw.By Sunday morning, police had detained 117 people across Poland for carrying knives or other dangerous weapons, or for threatening attacks against schools or fellow students. Authorities had checked around 64,000 schools, according to AP.Speaking at a crisis meeting with government and security officials on Sunday, Tusk said the school attacks were “spontaneous acts” driven by the online “glorification of violence”.“We are not dealing with any group organized on a big scale,” he said, adding that authorities had observed a rise in the fascination with violence both in Poland and globally.Tusk said some of those detained were active in far-right circles. He also pointed to increased online searches for Nazi-related content and mass killers who had become idols on the internet.Concerns over wider security threatsPoland has also raised concerns about security risks linked to its proximity to the war in Ukraine. In September, Tusk warned that Russia was likely to intensify hybrid attacks against Nato’s eastern flank.In August, police detained a 23-year-old man accused of calling for the assassination of senior Polish politicians, Reuters reported.Tusk had also said in 2024 that he received threats following the assassination attempt on Slovak Prime Minister Robert Fico.The latest security meeting comes amid concerns about possible copycat violence following the school attacks. Rumours of coordinated incidents and further attacks on what was described online as “bloody Friday” had circulated in parents’ online groups and mainstream media.As a result, 59 schools suspended classes pre-emptively on Friday, most of them in the Mazovian province.Tusk said police checks at schools would continue into next week. He also urged parents and teachers to talk to children about their online experiences and the consequences of becoming involved in online communities that glorify violence.Authorities have not disclosed further details about the reported threat against Tusk and Kosiniak-Kamysz.You use AI every day. articles.title: Pope Leo announces tumor on lung, surgery planned in 'next few days'
articles.summary: Pope Leo XIV announced doctors found a lung nodule at a "very early stage," with surgery scheduled in coming days.
articles.body: Pope Leo XIV announced Sunday that he will undergo surgery to remove a small nodule from his lung, revealing the unexpected health concern to thousands of faithful gathered in St. Peter's Square following his traditional Angelus prayer. The 71-year-old pontiff said doctors discovered the nodule at a "very early stage" and recommended its removal. The surgery is scheduled for the coming days, with the pope expected to remain hospitalized for approximately one week, according to Vatican spokesman Matteo Bruni. "Doctors found a small lump in the lung," Leo said after the Angelus address. "It was identified at a very early stage and well situated." POPE LEO VISITS SITE OF MIRACLE CURES, MEETS PEOPLE WHOSE UNEXPLAINED HEALINGS STUNNED DOCTORS "The doctors consider it appropriate to intervene and so, following their advice, I decided to have surgery to remove it," he continued. "The surgery is already scheduled for the next few days. I thank you for your spiritual closeness and I rely on your prayer." The surgery is likely to take place within a few days at the Gemelli Hospital in Rome, which is known as the "Pope's" hospital, Vatican sources told Fox News. The Vatican has not disclosed whether the nodule is cancerous, and no further details about the pope's diagnosis or the planned procedure were immediately available. The announcement comes as a surprise for the American-born pontiff, who has no previously known health problems and is known for maintaining an active lifestyle. Leo regularly plays tennis and swims at the papal summer retreat in Castel Gandolfo, according to The Associated Press. POPE LEO CALLS OUT ‘FALSE COMPASSION’ OF MEDICALLY ASSISTED SUICIDE DURING FRENCH HOSPITAL VISIT The pope is also scheduled to embark on a major international trip from Nov. 6–17, with planned stops in Uruguay, Argentina and Peru. It remains unclear whether his surgery and recovery will affect those travel plans. In addition to addressing his health, Leo used his Sunday remarks to renew his appeal for peace in war-torn Ukraine, warning that the conflict continues to inflict suffering far beyond the country's borders. "The war in the martyred Ukraine continues to create suffering, even beyond its borders, especially in the poorest countries, where many people depend on the exports of cereals and grains," the pope said. Leo called on those involved in the conflict to ensure the safe passage of Ukrainian grain shipments through the Black Sea, emphasizing the consequences for vulnerable populations around the world. articles.summary: HYDERABAD: A five-year-old girl was kidnapped and killed by a security guard who had been dismissed from his job at a gated community, Villa Orchids, in
articles.body: HYDERABAD: A five-year-old girl was kidnapped and killed by a security guard who had been dismissed from his job at a gated community, Villa Orchids, in Kowkoor, Bollaram, late on Saturday night. The accused continued to demand ransom throughout the night, keeping the girl’s family in the dark about her murder.Bollaram police said the victim, Aurelia, had gone to the clubhouse to watch the Bathukamma celebrations organised by the gated community.At 7.45 pm, her grandfather received a phone call from an unknown person claiming that their son was in his custody.“Aapka beta mere paas hai. Mujhe 20 lakh chahiye. Main Secunderabad mein hoon, aake le lo,” the caller said before disconnecting. However, when the girl’s brother was found cycling, their grandfather confronted the caller.The caller later contacted the girl’s father, Milton Fernandes Moses, a research scientist at an agriculture-based company, claiming that his daughter was in his captivity.As the girl had not returned from the Bathukamma celebrations, her family members rushed to the clubhouse but could not find her.“Earlier, celebrations were being held with music and other activities, and the girl went to watch them. At 7.30 pm, when she did not return, I asked my son to call her home. After some time, my son returned home and said she would be back in five minutes,” the mother recalled.Panicked, the victim’s family told the accused that they could not pay the large amount demanded and requested him to reduce the ransom. The accused asked them to transfer the money to a bank account. Willing to pay the ransom, the family asked him to at least show the girl on a video call to reassure them of her safety. However, the accused refused their request.After some time, the victim’s family informed the police, who reached the spot. Subsequently, the accused’s phone was switched off. Meanwhile, residents of the gated community checked CCTV footage, which showed the girl leaving the clubhouse. A short distance away, a man was seen following her.When the police and residents traced the phone number from which the victim’s family had received the call, they found that it belonged to a security guard on duty at the gated community. During questioning, the guard claimed that Vikram, a native of Bihar who had been dismissed from his job, had entered the premises. He said Vikram had used his phone to make the ransom calls. In one of the CCTV clips, Vikram was seen signalling something to the guard while hurriedly leaving the premises.Based on information provided by the guard on duty late on Saturday night, residents and police searched the clubhouse cellar, where the girl’s body was found in a water sump. Her hands and legs were tied, and two bricks had been tied around her waist. The incident has sent shock waves through the community.Police have taken all the security guards currently working at the gated community into custody for questioning. Meanwhile, police deployed drones in Secunderabad and other parts of the city to trace Vikram, who is wanted in connection with the case. Special teams were also sent to Patancheru and other areas in search of the accused.The heartbroken family demanded justice and urged officials to punish the accused. “I want the accused to die,” the victim’s mother said in anger.Vikram had been removed from his job by the society a few days ago over allegations of poor conduct.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Hyderabad | Silver Rate in Hyderabad | Bank Holidays in Hyderabad | Public Holidays in Hyderabad | Hyderabad AQI | Weather in Hyderabad | Petrol Price in Hyderabad | Diesel Price in Hyderabad | CNG Price in Hyderabad | LPG Price in HyderabadStay updated with the latest Hyderabad news. articles.title: Yorkshire Wildlife Park remains closed after fatal tiger attack
articles.summary: Yorkshire Wildlife Park remains closed after a man entered the tiger enclosure and was fatally attacked on Saturday.
articles.body:
Yorkshire Wildlife Park remains closed after a man climbed into a tiger enclosure and was fatally attacked by the animal.

Emergency services were called to the park near Doncaster, South Yorkshire, at about 13:30 BST on Saturday after reports of a man climbing down into the enclosure from a walkway.

An eyewitness described seeing the man wearing headphones and "pacing around" near the enclosure before he went in and was attacked. Police said the man sadly died at the scene.

A park spokesperson said their "thoughts and heartfelt sympathies" remain with the man's family and confirmed the Amur tiger, called Altai, remained in the enclosure and would not be euthanised.

The spokesperson says many people had contacted them about the tiger and he was safe and well.

Staff who were at the scene who were "deeply affected by events" would receive specialist support, they added.

South Yorkshire Police said the man's family were being supported by officers. "Our thoughts are with them at this distressing time," the force said in a statement.

It added: "We are aware of videos circulating online and we would encourage people not to share this footage."

Earlier on Saturday, in a statement posted on its website, the park said its emergency response procedures had been "immediately activated" and it was "working closely with the authorities to ascertain exactly what happened".

Ella Ford, 24, from Moreton, Wirral, had visited the park with her boyfriend and filmed the tiger moments before the attack.

She described seeing a man by the tiger enclosure "pacing around with his headphones in".

A few minutes later, she saw the same man had "climbed up onto the barriers".

A woman was close by talking to him, she said, before "he jumped in and crawled in front of the tiger, where the tiger was perched and just lay there".

Ford said she then witnessed the tiger grab hold of the man, who she reported as "shouting for help".

She estimates around 15 to 20 people were on the enclosure's raised visitor walkway before staff quickly evacuated the area, and shortly afterwards, the park.

She described members of the public as being "confused, like what on earth's going on?"

"I just know some man was obviously trying to bang on the fence to try and deter the tiger away, but it obviously wasn't doing anything," she said.

Karmelle Pelham, 39, from Worksop, had been enjoying a family day out when park staff told them the site was being evacuated.

She said she had heard what sounded like "gunshots" and an air ambulance had circled above.

Pelham added: "There was a big, black tarpaulin over the tiger enclosure."

She praised park staff for their handling of the incident, saying it had been "very, very well organised".

Foreign Secretary and MP for Doncaster North Ed Miliband said he was "deeply saddened" to hear of the incident and sent his "thoughts and deepest condolences to the family of the individual who died."

He added he was "very grateful to the emergency services and staff of the park who responded."

Lee Pitcher, MP for Doncaster East and the Isle of Axholme, expressed his gratitude to emergency services for their response.

In a statement shared to social media, he said he was "deeply saddened to hear about the tragic incident that has taken place at Yorkshire Wildlife Park today".

Yorkshire Wildlife Park opened in 2009, with its Land of the Tigers area opening in 2011.

The purpose-built two-acre reserve is home to Amur tigers, an endangered subspecies with around 500 left in the wild.

Photos of the enclosure on the park's website shows a high walkway for visitors and fencing above the section where the tigers can roam.
